summary: Clarify dual-quota strategy for background flushes vs interactive requests during sustained spikes
description:
Issue summary:
NimbleAuth (dedicated customer) is seeing recurring 429 throttles during nightly background database flushes that coincide with daytime interactive traffic. They believe background workers are consuming burst credits and causing short-lived 429s for their low-latency endpoints. They asked for prescriptive guidance: how to split quota between background and interactive workloads, how dual-window accounting works, and recommended configs for a dedicated pool with predictable throughput.

Impact:
- Intermittent 429s on interactive API routes during overlapping windows of bulk background flushes.
- Customer reports degraded UX for end-users and internal alarms firing. No data loss reported; mostly retries and latency spikes.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in prod us-east (pool-73)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs scheduled nightly flush job (multipart bulk insert) between 09:00-10:30 UTC.
2) Simultaneously their interactive traffic peaks from EU users hitting replica endpoints proxied through us-east.
3) Observed behavior: background job consumes burst window; interactive requests receive 429s for 10-30s bursts despite overall quota still present for day-level capacity.
4) Retry patterns from the client amplify transient window exhaustion.
expected_behavior: Background flushes should be isolated from interactive low-latency routes either via separate per-route quotas or prioritized weighting so that interactive requests do not receive 429s during scheduled bulk work.
observed_behavior: Short 429 bursts on interactive endpoints during background job windows. Token/burst accounting appears to be shared at pool/tenant level and the customer cannot enforce per-route isolation for their worker processes.
logs_and_traces: Attached tenant throttle heatmap (link) and example request traces showing 429 responses with X-RateLimit-* headers. Edge logs show burst token burn: token_window=60s, burst_used=100% for pool-73 between 09:12-09:18 UTC.
temporary_workaround_requested: Customer asked for immediate mitigations: 1) best practice config to reduce interaction 429s tonight, 2) recommended backoff/retry settings for bulk worker to avoid retry storms.

Suggested immediate mitigations in comment: 1) throttle worker concurrency to 25% of current, 2) add jittered exponential backoff starting at 200ms, 3) schedule background flush to off-peak hours or pin to a sub-route with lower weight.

2026-03-12 11:12 - Customer (NimbleAuth - Daniel Cho): Tried suggested worker cap + jitter; saw 80% reduction in interactive 429s during a second test window but still occasional spikes. Asked whether a recommended per-route separate quota is enforceable on dedicated pools.

2026-03-12 13:00 - Priya Kapur: Confirmed per-route isolation can be configured on Dedicated but needs a support ops change and may affect billing accounting. Escalating to Product for guidance and creating follow-up internal task INT-4421.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The dedicated pool exposes two refill windows: a short token window (60s) for burst capacity and a longer smoothing window for sustained throughput. Background flushes use many concurrent connections that exhaust the short window; retries from the flush amplify counts via connection reuse misattribution. SRE checks show health-check probes and worker heartbeats incremented accounting for pool-73, increasing token consumption. Next steps: 1) verify per-route quota enforcement for this customer, 2) reproduce with a controlled background job in staging using same concurrency, 3) propose config template for dual-window separation and worker backoff defaults.
resolution: Workaround provided: recommended worker concurrency cap, jittered backoff, and rescheduling to off-peak which reduced 429s. Product validated that dedicated pools support per-route quota separation but require a config change and billing flag. Follow-up: Create INT-4421 to schedule a dedicated-pool quota isolation rollout for NimbleAuth and produce a short runbook. Owner: Priya Kapur. Planned permanent fix: reserve a small per-route burst allocation for interactive routes and place bulk workers on a separate route with a capped sustained window. Status: pending change window approval.
next_steps: 1) Open change request for pool-73 to enable per-route quota separation (INT-4421). 2) Share runbook with customer that includes example rate-limiter rules and worker retry config. 3) Monitor next scheduled flush and iterate. Assigned to: Priya Kapur.
